## Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR #194, exact head `f4d0e459579f4decb7a6023e204d575898e80e21`.

The complete changed-code diff and directly dependent caller-ID admission paths were source-reviewed. No high-confidence new security vulnerability was identified. The verdict covers the 29 reserved namespaces, not an exhaustive guarantee about every possible daemon-generated ID.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No new vulnerability identified | - |

### Reservation and ingress

`NoticeKind` lists 29 fixed prefixes and uses exact prefix concatenation/starts_with (`crates/core/src/notice_id.rs:84-166`).

`/v1/send` rejects reserved caller IDs before peer/local branching, role routing, FYI holding, controls or queue mutation (`crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1949-2003`). Peer origin comes from its credential rather than the body. Inbound federation posts to this same guarded endpoint; peer credentials cannot use shim/sidecar/local mutation routes (`crates/daemon/src/federation/mod.rs:533-536`; `http/mod.rs:471-503`).

Telegram and document variants check their request IDs before enqueue/document staging (`http/mod.rs:4635-4657`). Document numbering only appends a suffix and cannot create a reserved prefix afterward (`crates/sidecars/src/telegram_document.rs:290-293`). The refusal renders the supplied ID through `render::msg_id`, not raw text (`http/mod.rs:2349-2360`).

Shim does not call the guard, but it mints hexadecimal message IDs internally and refuses unknown flags; callers cannot supply a message ID (`crates/daemon/src/http/shim.rs:392,677,700,711`; `crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:2420-2422`). Native Copilot/OMP/Pi mint their IDs and send through the guarded endpoint. ACK and UDS reply paths refer to existing claims/jobs rather than admitting a new caller-selected ledger identity.

### Case and encoding

JSON escapes are decoded before reservation checking. Case variants, Unicode lookalikes/normalization variants and literal percent-encoding do not bypass reservation for an equal notice key: they are different exact keys. The traced storage paths perform no case folding, Unicode normalization or URL decoding (`crates/store/migrations/0028_message_origin.sql:7-33`; `crates/store/src/queue.rs:582-617,1220-1248`). Origin remains a separate identity field.

### Coverage and compatibility notes

The static gate is a lexical source-shape scan, not exhaustive data-flow enforcement (`crates/daemon/tests/notice_ids.rs:17-35,88-155`). It can miss alternate constructions or arbitrary argument expressions. Unchanged general-mint routing FYIs and legacy background-sidecar constructions prevent a blanket assertion that all daemon-authored IDs use these 29 kinds; no bypass into the protected prefixes was demonstrated through them.

Withdrawal now uses the reserved request-withdrawn prefix (`crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:1159`). An old `<id>.withdrawn` FYI would not deduplicate the new key, so an upgrade-spanning retry can produce an extra notice. The reported zero-old-row live-store count was not independently checked; this verdict does not claim universal old-ID compatibility.

No new C19/C21 disclosure was identified. GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42518488459` and Delivers run `42518488352` both identify this SHA and success.

No local tests, builds, mutations, runtime sends/federation traffic, sidecar operations, credential reads or payload execution were performed. Claimed mutation controls were not independently repeated.
